title: Bolder hand · HC Tracking
question: Image previews are unavailable (the OpenAI account has no credits), so cards show layout wireframes. Foreign forms at full commitment, each fused with your product; red/gray, Somar Sans and the sidebar still hold. The deal leads with the Darkroom. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Darkroom
options.lineage: Printing darkroom under safelight: enlarger, timed baths, drying line
options.thesis: Work develops through fixed stations under your own red safelight, and a finished record is a print you can trust.
materials: white enamel print sheets for finished records
test strips that preview before commit
options.viewport: Dashboard as the darkroom bench: a station rail across the top (Proposed → Approved → Delivering → Reporting → Closed) with counts in timer digits; below, records develop into sharp prints as they load; approved reports hang on a drying line.
options.risk: A red-washed dark ground can feel oppressive and weaken contrast; the safelight must stay on stations and moments, never flood the working surface.

raised.raise: Every record carries one fixed end-label grid (name, variant, key figure), so a stack of records scans by its edge alone.
Every change narrates its consequence in words ("Tranche 2 marked received · EUR 40,000 now disbursed"), and it stays reversible until it's fixed.

options.label: Construction Grid
options.thesis: The portfolio is built cell by cell on a visible grid: one cell per project, and the figures themselves are drawn from the grid.
materials: one red accent plane per page
options.viewport: Dashboard as a specimen sheet: giant grid-constructed portfolio figures, each program a block of unit cells coloured by status, all on a visible grid.
options.case: Holds clarity (grid discipline and huge legible figures) but loses identification: the audience doesn't know this design tradition.
options.risk: Monumental numerals can crowd out dense officer workflows if the scale isn't disciplined.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Every transfer, target and task rendered as one bar in a dense field: the whole portfolio visible at once, sharpening into exact figures on selection.
options.viewport: Dashboard as a wall of bars, one per record; selecting a column pulls its exact figures into focus while the field dims.
options.case: Holds clarity for dense scanning of figures, but identification is low and it breaks Somar Sans's warmth.
options.risk: Can read as art installation; strobing must be off entirely for daily use.

options.label: Wall Calendar Pad
options.lineage: Printing-house advertising calendars with tear-off pads
options.thesis: Time is the axis your office already lives by: deadlines on a tear-off pad beneath a field-work plate.
options.viewport: Dashboard as this month's leaf: deadlines in date cells, today ringed, past dates grayed, a field photograph above.
options.case: Holds identification (every NGO office has one on the wall) but loses clarity for money and the logframe.
options.risk: Needs real field photography you'd have to supply; time-only structure strains non-dated pages.

options.label: Archive Box Wall
options.thesis: Records as boxes you pull from a stack.
options.viewport: Donors and projects as a stacked wall of labelled box ends.
options.case: Fuses poorly: its orange ground overrides the brand, and box-pulling slows daily work.
options.kept: One fixed end-label grid on every record.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.viewport: Status changes as typographic weather events.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no identification; motion obscures figures and Arabic text.
options.kept: Every change narrates its consequence in words.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A best-in-class SaaS operations dashboard, in your brand colours.
canonCard.viewport: KPI card row, two charts, then a recent-activity table.
canonCard.risk: Polished, but indistinguishable from every other admin dashboard, which you asked to avoid.
